handled_verified._description: Every node type real-clean-analyzer.ts compares against, each one exercised by a committed fixture — this list is evidence only because the F6 gate parses the fixtures and reports any type no parse tree contains. Fixtures: definition-module-interface.dcl (the declaration contract, four signature_name shapes), signature-definition-merge.icl (the declaration/definition merge, an operator callable and its scope exit), instance-target-name-collision.icl (a type colliding with an instance for it), expression-shapes.icl (case, lambda, guards, where block, list comprehension, qualified call, records, class/instance), import-modules-alias-884.icl (comma-separated imports).

internal_silent._description: Structural wrappers, type-tree internals and literals that correctly emit nothing. A type_signature is a TYPE tree, so the walk skips its children wholesale (no call site can live inside one) — strict_type/type_application/type_variable are traversed, never dispatched on. local_binding wraps a where-local, which is scoped noise by contract (M11.11): its body attributes to no caller and its signature publishes no symbol.

gap._description: Named worklists, not hidden ones. The differential does not depend on any of them (F5 is 0 MISSING / 0 UNEXPLAINED exhaustively over all 312 corpus files of the lane's five bases), so each gap is a coverage statement, not a correctness claim.

gaps.missing: the three node types introduced in v1.2.7 that this analyzer names nowhere. They are lexer-level refinements of shapes the analyzer already handles through other nodes (`>>=`, array generators, `[1..]`), so nothing is lost today; the gap is that their arrival is not measured by any fixture. The fourth new type, char_list, is classified internal_silent above because it wraps a literal.

inline `code { ... }` machine-code blocks (clean-stdlib/_SystemDynamic.icl) are not parseable Clean, so the whole file carries ERROR nodes and nothing inside them can be attributed honestly. This is the lane's single grammar-error file on the five bases (F10: Clyde 17 of 109 files damaged, clean-stdlib 1 of 74, and every one of them is a deliberate, classified residual rather than a silent drop). Same category as Go's testdata and Haskell's TemplateHaskell quasiquotes.

a class declaration's CONTEXT (`class Eq a | == a`) is not modelled: the constraint identifiers publish nothing and emit no edge. Measured on clean-stdlib/StdClass.dcl, where the whole file is class declarations with contexts.

design_decision.description: The Clean FP-family contract, each ruling probe- or fixture-verified (see the fixtures named in handled_verified, plus script/m14/tmp/clean-fixture-probe.ts and the four CLEAN probes of the F9 battery).

decisions.question: are bare value reads emitted as `uses`?
decisions.resolution: No — the FP-family contract (Clojure/Elixir/Erlang/Haskell precedent): variable references are noise. The lane emits contains/implements/calls/instantiates/references only.

decisions.question: what does a module-level signature publish, given that a `.dcl` is declarations only?
decisions.resolution: A Function symbol marked `metadata.isDeclaration`, keyed `::name`. A later in-file definition REPLACES it (one entity, the definition's range) — the C prototype/definition merge, real-c-analyzer.ts. Class/instance member signatures are already Method symbols from the class/instance path; a where-local signature publishes nothing.

decisions.question: is an operator definition a callable, and where does its attribution stop?
decisions.resolution: It is a callable wherever it lives (module level, instance member, class member), so its body's applications attribute to the operator's unparenthesized name. Inside a where block it is scoped noise, and a comma/brace pattern mis-shape (`# (a,b,c) = e;`, `(r,{gst & ls=s})`) names nothing. The attribution is RELEASED when the operator's scope exits: before that fix the operator stayed `currentFunction` and swallowed the next module-level application (`calls ++| -> flatten` in clean-stdlib/StdOverloadedList.icl).

decisions.question: what is an instance named, and what happens when the name collides with its target type?
decisions.resolution: Named after the TARGET type (the universal impl-naming contract: Rust `impl User`, Elixir `defimpl`, Haskell `instance ... User`), and `implements targetType -> className`. A file that also defines that type therefore offers the name twice; the export list is deduped by NAME first-wins (the type, which comes first, is the importable unit) because the exports-family invariant requires a name a duplicate cannot identify its provider for.

decisions.question: does a record emit an instantiation, and what do its fields publish?
decisions.resolution: Fields publish Property symbols owned by their type and are contained by it. A record CONSTRUCTION or UPDATE emits no `instantiates` — only a constructor-headed application does, so a record literal is never an instantiation.

decisions.question: which guard shapes are decision points for cyclomatic complexity?
decisions.resolution: Both, and they are different things: `guard_equation` is a function guard (1,594 sites over the five bases) and `guard` is a list-comprehension qualifier (23 sites, every one under a comprehension_qualifier). The counter used to read `guard` alone, so it measured comprehension filters while every function guard went uncounted.

decisions.question: where does pattern territory end inside a function definition?
decisions.resolution: At the body FIELD: everything before it is a pattern, so a constructor there never becomes `instantiates`. The pre-fix gate tested each child for `type === "operator" && text === "="`, which this grammar cannot produce (a definition's children are name/pattern…/body and the `=` is not a child; the 1,576 corpus `operator` nodes are operator symbols under binary_expression/unary_expression/paren_pattern), so the gate was dead — a grammar that app-lifts a head pattern would have started fabricating with nothing in the way.

decisions.question: what is exported from a module that has no export keyword?
decisions.resolution: The module-level symbols: `ownerName === currentModule` (or ownerless) — the haskell rule, since the module is the namespace and `import M (f)` binds `f` — restricted to exportable kinds and deduped by name. Measured over the five bases: 4,443 exports over 305 of 312 files; the 7 without one are the `_`-prefixed compiler-internal modules, whose names are private by Clean convention. The predicate used to be `!sym.ownerName`, the exact negation of the rule its own comment stated, which left 312 of 312 files exporting at most one thing.
